title: DOM events and handlers
summary: Respond to user input with event listeners and state updates.

scenario.briefing: The Add to cart button has no behavior. Implement the handler logic that toggles the cart count and returns the new count.

objectives.description: Implement an event handler that updates state.

hints: Keep cart state in a variable.
let count = 0; function addToCart() { count += 1; return count; }

misconceptions.description: Putting large logic in inline onclick attributes.
misconceptions.feedback: Inline handlers mix structure and behavior. Attach listeners in script and keep handlers testable.
Events bubble by default; stopPropagation is only needed when a parent must not react.

sections.title: Events
sections.body: The browser emits events for user actions. addEventListener attaches a handler. The handler receives an event object and can update state.

sections.title: State and rendering
sections.body: Event handlers should update a single source of truth and let rendering follow. Keep handlers small and testable by extracting pure logic.

vocabulary.definition: A function called when an event occurs.
An event traveling from target up to ancestors.
The browser's built-in response to an event.
